arxiv-2405-09446.title: M 4 oE: A Foundation Model for Medical Multimodal Image Segmentation with Mixture of Experts
arxiv-2405-09446.creator: Yufeng Jiang, Yiqing Shen (✉)
arxiv-2405-09446.description: Abstract Medical imaging data is inherently heterogeneous across different modalities and clinical centers, posing unique challenges for developing generalizable foundation models. Conventional entails training distinct models per dataset or using a shared encoder with modality-specific decoders. However, these approaches incur heavy computational overheads and suffer from poor scalability.

arxiv-2408-05832.title: Compact majority-minority districts almost never exist
arxiv-2408-05832.creator: Boris Alexeev, Dustin G. Mixon
arxiv-2408-05832.description: Abstract For a uniformly distributed population, we show that with high probability, any majority-minority voting district containing a fraction of the population necessarily exhibits a tiny Polsby–Popper score. 1 Introduction Gerrymandering is the manipulation of voting district boundaries to favor a party or class.

arxiv-2410-05963.title: Training-Free Open-Ended Object Detection and Segmentation via Attention as Prompts
arxiv-2410-05963.creator: Zhiwei Lin, Yongtao Wang, Zhi Tang
arxiv-2410-05963.description: Abstract Existing perception models achieve great success by learning from large amounts of labeled data, but they still struggle with open-world scenarios. To alleviate this issue, researchers introduce open-set perception tasks to detect or segment unseen objects in the training set. However, these models require predefined object categories as inputs during inference, which are not available in real-world scenarios.

arxiv-2412-17009.title: Generate to Discriminate: Expert Routing for Continual Learning
arxiv-2412-17009.creator: Yewon Byun 1, Sanket Vaibhav Mehta 1, Saurabh Garg 1,2, Emma Strubell 1, Michael Oberst 3, Bryan Wilder 1, Zachary C. Lipton 1
arxiv-2412-17009.description: Abstract In many real-world settings, regulations and economic incentives permit the sharing of models but not data across institutional boundaries. In such scenarios, practitioners might hope to adapt models to new domains, without losing performance on previous domains (so-called catastrophic forgetting).

arxiv-2501-11929.title: ALoFTRAG: Automatic Local Fine Tuning for Retrieval Augmented Generation
arxiv-2501-11929.creator: Peter Devine
arxiv-2501-11929.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Peter Devine. Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) systems have been shown to improve the accuracy of Large Language Model (LLM) outputs. However, these models can often achieve low accuracy when applied to new data domains. We introduce the Automatic Local Fine Tuning of Retrieval Augmented Generation models (ALoFTRAG) framework, designed to improve the accuracy of RAG systems on a given domain by training LLMs without manually labeled data or using larger teacher models.

arxiv-2505-10399.title: Evaluating Model Explanations without Ground Truth
arxiv-2505-10399.creator: Kaivalya Rawal, Zihao Fu, Eoin Delaney, Chris Russell
arxiv-2505-10399.description: Abstract . There can be many competing and contradictory explanations for a single model prediction, making it difficult to select which one to use. Current explanation evaluation frameworks measure quality by comparing against ideal “ground-truth” explanations, or by verifying model sensitivity to important inputs.

arxiv-2506-15377.title: Efficient and Generalizable Environmental Understanding for Visual Navigation
arxiv-2506-15377.creator: Ruoyu Wang, Xinshu Li, Chen Wang, Lina Yao
arxiv-2506-15377.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ruoyu Wang, Xinshu Li, Chen Wang, Lina Yao. Visual Navigation is a core task in Embodied AI, enabling agents to navigate complex environments toward given objectives. Across diverse settings within Navigation tasks, many necessitate the modelling of sequential data accumulated from preceding time steps. While existing methods perform well, they typically process all historical observations simultaneously, overlooking the internal association structure within the data, which may limit the potential for further improvements in task performance.

arxiv-2601-21631.title: Turning Language Model Training from Black Box into a Sandbox PubID: pubid: 000-0-0000-0000-0/00/$00.00 ©2026 IEEE Thanks: This study was funded by the Strategic Research Council (SRC) established within the Research Council of Finland, grant #352859.
arxiv-2601-21631.creator: Nicolas Pope, Matti Tedre
arxiv-2601-21631.description: Abstract Most classroom engagements with generative AI focus on prompting pre-trained models, leaving the role of training data and model mechanics opaque. We developed a browser-based tool that allows students to train a small transformer language model entirely on their own device, making the training process visible.

pmc-13067105.title: Gauging lipid vulnerabilities in mRNA-LNPs under various environmental stressors through TIMS-TOF analysis

pmc-13067105.description: The long-term stability of mRNA lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) is governed by the chemical resilience of their constituent lipids, yet the specific degradation pathways triggered by real-world stressors remain poorly defined. Here, we systematically mapped lipid-specific vulnerabilities in mRNA-LNPs formulated with three clinically relevant ionizable lipids, DLin-MC3-DMA (MC3), SM-102, and ALC-0315, under controlled thermal, photo-oxidative, and mechanical stress conditions.

pmc-13289495.title: Postoperative pain management after VATS for spontaneous pneumothorax - a systematic review

pmc-13289495.description: BackgroundHistorically, thoracic epidural analgesia has been the standard for postoperative pain management after surgery for spontaneous pneumothorax. With the advent of enhanced recovery after thoracic surgery protocols, less invasive locoregional analgesic techniques are increasingly considered. Due to lack of high-quality evidence, current guidelines do not address optimal analgesic strategies in this population.
